LAPH teams in support of regulation 3 of the NHS (Control of Patient Information) Regulations 2002 to provide Public Health services require HES data. The LAPH activities which the data will support are: 
• Monitoring and analysing trends in communicable disease and other risks to public health • Joint Strategic Needs Assessment 
• Health Needs Assessments • Measuring health inequalities • Health surveillance & monitoring • Monitoring and analysing trends in communicable disease and other risks to public health • Identification of presentations of cancer including early presentations in order to assess the effectiveness of screening interventions and the success of screening programmes.
 • Evidence to understand the impact of environmental and planning factors (for example alcohol licensing, gambling, fast food restaurant and leisure enhancements) 
• Assess the levels of disease and injury for example childhood injury and self harm Analysis and manipulation of the data In order to carry out the analyses described above, the hospital data received from HSCIC, will be analysed at record level to be able to: • Split it by population groups such as age, gender, ethnicity, deprivation; and • Split by geography to determine which cohorts are at most at risk of poor health outcomes and inequitable service provision; 
• Analyse historic data (LAPH teams are also required to assess change in disease prevalence over time for different groups) Linking of data The data will not be linked to other data sources. Onward transmission of data There will be no onward transmission of the data. Publishing data 
• The analysis above will be used to produce non-sensitive, non-identifiable outputs such as, summary reports and data trend graphs. These may be be published, inline with the data protection legislation detailed in section 9 of this contract, and the contract requirements detailed in section 5 of this contract. These publications inform health and care services, interventions and policy and strategy. • 
• Based on your Re-Use Application statement (above), the HSCIC grants to Licensee a non-exclusive licence to use or re-use the data specified in section 3 above for the following purposes: 
• Use only within the Field and Territory as specified in this Agreement. • Publishing the material in any medium, including featuring the information asset on websites which can be accessed via the Internet or via an internal electronic network or on an Intranet. • Authorising users and subscribers who use the Licensee’s electronic or digital products to access the material. • To share non-sensitive, non-identifiable outputs from the purposes detailed above within data protection legislation detailed under section 9 of this contract and contract requirements detailed in section 5 of this contract, in order to inform health and care services, interventions and policy and strategy.
